claim: A staging area is only an unused piece of land.

claim: Homo sapiens are endangered.

claim: Ron Weasley is only part of the Game of Thrones series.

claim: Bruce Shand was unable to earn the Military Cross.

claim: Baz Luhrmann only has films from 2007.

claim: Norman Bates is a fictional character.

claim: Aldous Huxley published writings.

claim: Yvonne Strahovski worked on an ABC show.

claim: Janelle Monáe is Canadian.

claim: The Maze Runner's budget was $34 million.

claim: The Tracey Fragments had its North American premiere somewhere other than at a film festival.

claim: Freddie Highmore has been nominated for the Critics' Choice Television Award.

claim: Weekly Idol is hosted by Jeong Hyeong-don.

claim: The highest point of the Hindu Kush is Tirich Mir in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

claim: Floyd Mayweather Jr. has made 30 career boxing knockouts in different special event professional boxing fights.

claim: South Island is divided from North Island by Cook Strait.

claim: The X-Files starred Harrison Ford.

claim: Queen (band) is a Canadian rock band.

claim: The Cretaceous is yet to end.

claim: The Concert for Bangladesh raised close to $250,000 for Haiti relief.

claim: Resident Evil is the first installment in the Resident Evil video game series.

claim: Advertising is used to sell a way of doing things.

claim: Match Point was a film by Woody Allen.

claim: LinkedIn is based on Earth.

claim: You Only Live Twice was directed by a German man.

claim: Moscovium is atomic symbol Pb.

claim: Sleipnir is an animal.

claim: Mary of Teck's son married a Wallis Simpson.

claim: The cinematography of Far from the Madding Crowd was by an Spanish film director.

claim: Live Through This is only a short story.

claim: The 1976 thriller Duel was Steven Spielberg's directorial debut.

claim: Virginia's largest export by monetary value is a computer component.

claim: The Mirny (sloop-of-war) was in expedition.

claim: Paul Nicholls did not play Joe Wicks.

claim: I Kissed a Girl was only recorded by an American bassist.

claim: The Times is a website.

claim: Sennacherib's youngest son was Ismael.

claim: Benjamin Walker (actor) is a thespian.

claim: Emmanuel Macron worked as an investment banker.

claim: The Bengal tiger is a member of the largest cat species.
response_text: TRUE.  Tigers (Panthera tigris) are the largest cat species, and the Bengal tiger is a subspecies of tiger (Panthera tigris tigris). Note: the Amur/Siberian tiger is typically the largest subspecies, but tigers overall are the largest cats.

claim: Two and a Half Men is an British television sitcom.

claim: The Road to El Dorado only stars Ben Stiller.

claim: Aldous Huxley published film scripts.

claim: "Dog" is Duane Chapman's nickname.

claim: There is a show called The Office (US).

claim: Tijuana is on an island.

claim: The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie only stars Donald Trump.

claim: Pythagoras is unassociated with Pythagoras' ideas.
response_text: FALSE.  By definition, “Pythagoras’ ideas” are associated with Pythagoras. claim: Catherine Hardwicke has been unable to ever do any production design.

claim: CHiPs is an American action novel.

claim: Alexandria is the largest seaport in Egypt.
response_text: TRUE.  The Port of Alexandria (including El Dekheila) is widely cited as Egypt’s main and largest seaport, handling the largest share of the country’s foreign trade. claim: The Hunchback of Notre Dame is notable only for its cast.
response_text: FALSE.  Beyond its cast, The Hunchback of Notre Dame is notable for its source (Victor Hugo’s classic novel), themes, and multiple celebrated craft elements across adaptations: landmark makeup and sets (1923), acclaimed production design and score (1939), and the 1996 Disney film’s praised animation and Alan Menken score. claim: David Veloz heavily revised the screenplay for Natural Born Killers.
response_text: TRUE.  David Veloz is one of the three credited screenwriters (with Oliver Stone and Richard Rutowski) on Natural Born Killers. claim: Homer Hickman is illiterate.

claim: Sean Penn has acted in 13 films.

claim: The retreat of permafrost is an expected outcome of global warming.

claim: Unison (Celine Dion album) was originally released by Warner Music Group.

claim: See You on the Other Side was certified platinum on March 8, 2006.

claim: George III of the United Kingdom had experiences.

claim: A monk practices religious asceticism.

claim: Veeru Devgan choreographs stunts.

claim: Ludwig van Beethoven was part of the jam band era.

claim: Sacre-Coeur, Paris is an embodiment of conservative ethical order.

claim: Pink is an actress.

claim: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic was in an international organization.

claim: Solanum contains the horse nettles.

claim: Physics' main goal is to observe the behavior of the universe.

claim: Birthday Song (2 Chainz song) was banned by Mike Dean.

claim: The Greek language is spoken only outside of Cyprus.

claim: See You on the Other Side was certified gold in the US in January 2016.

claim: Stephen Hillenburg has always hated the ocean.

claim: In the End has piano in it.

response_text: FALSE. Brubaker (1980), starring Robert Redford, is a serious prison drama about corruption and reform in an Arkansas penitentiary, not a comedy.

claim: Guatemala's civil war had two sides.
response_text: TRUE.  Explanation: In broad terms the Guatemalan Civil War (1960–1996) pitted the state (army, police, intelligence, and allied paramilitaries) against leftist guerrilla groups that later unified as the URNG. This is an oversimplification—there were multiple insurgent factions and state-aligned militias—but the conflict’s negotiations and peace accords were between these two broad sides.

claim: Faye Resnick works in interior design.
response_text: TRUE. Faye Resnick is known as an interior designer and runs Faye Resnick Design; she’s been described and featured in that role (e.g., on Real Housewives of Beverly Hills).

claim: Star Trek: Discovery is the first series since Star Trek: The Next Generation.
response_text: FALSE. After The Next Generation, several series aired before Discovery: Deep Space Nine (1993–1999), Voyager (1995–2001), and Enterprise (2001–2005). Discovery premiered in 2017.

claim: Elizabeth of York married in 1811.
response_text: FALSE.  Elizabeth of York (1466–1503), daughter of Edward IV, married Henry VII on 18 January 1486. The later Princess Elizabeth of York (the future Elizabeth II) married in 1947. No notable “Elizabeth of York” married in 1811.

claim: Asylum Records is an American record label founded in 1979 by David Geffen and partner Elliot Roberts.
response_text: FALSE.  Asylum Records is an American label founded in 1971 by David Geffen and Elliot Roberts, not 1979.

claim: The CONCACAF Champions League is almost an annual continental football club competition.
response_text: FALSE.  Explanation: The CONCACAF Champions League (2008–2023) was an annual continental club competition organized by CONCACAF, held every year (though formats and calendar timing changed). “Almost annual” is inaccurate.

claim: Ekta Kapoor worked on an Indian soap opera.
response_text: TRUE.  Ekta Kapoor is a prominent Indian TV producer known for creating and producing numerous Indian soap operas, including Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, Kahaani Ghar Ghar Kii, and Kasautii Zindagii Kay.

claim: On Nickelodeon SpongeBob SquarePants is the highest rated series to ever air.
response_text: TRUE.  SpongeBob SquarePants is widely cited as Nickelodeon’s highest‑rated and most-watched series in the network’s history, surpassing earlier leaders like Rugrats. Note: some single episodes of other shows (e.g., iCarly) have drawn higher one-off telecast numbers, but as a series overall SpongeBob holds the top spot.

claim: Fuller House (TV series) is a television series' sequel.
response_text: TRUE. Fuller House is a sequel/continuation of the TV series Full House, following the characters years later.

claim: Civilization IV received high ratings.
response_text: TRUE.  Civilization IV (2005) was widely acclaimed, holding a Metacritic score around 94/100 and earning 9+ ratings from major outlets (e.g., IGN and GameSpot both around 9.4/10), along with multiple year-end awards.

claim: Doxycycline may induce diarrhea.
response_text: TRUE. Doxycycline, like many antibiotics, commonly causes gastrointestinal side effects, including diarrhea, and can occasionally lead to antibiotic-associated diarrhea (e.g., C. difficile).

claim: The Stanford prison experiment was funded by an organization that coordinates, executes, and promotes the science and technology programs of the U.S. Army and Marine Corps.
response_text: FALSE.  The Stanford prison experiment was funded by the U.S. Office of Naval Research, which coordinates, executes, and promotes science and technology programs for the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps—not the Army.

claim: Hannah and Her Sisters ends with a Christmas dinner.
response_text: FALSE.  Hannah and Her Sisters is framed by family Thanksgiving dinners. It begins and ends with Thanksgiving at Hannah’s parents’ apartment, not Christmas.

claim: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic was a founding member of the UN.
response_text: TRUE.  The Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic signed the UN Charter in 1945 and became an original member (alongside the USSR and the Byelorussian SSR). Ukraine later continued this membership after 1991.

claim: Celebrity Rehab with Dr. Drew was a scripted TV drama.
response_text: FALSE.  Celebrity Rehab with Dr. Drew was a VH1 reality/docu-series following real patients’ addiction treatment, not a scripted TV drama.

claim: Marcus Bentley is an American broadcaster.
response_text: FALSE.  Marcus Bentley is English, best known as the UK Big Brother narrator. He was born in Stockton-on-Tees, England, not American.

claim: Sarah Hyland started acting in 2001.
response_text: FALSE. Sarah Hyland began acting in the late 1990s, with early credits including the film Private Parts (1997) and the TV movie Annie (1999), well before 2001.

claim: Tom Baker has reviewed video games.
response_text: FALSE.  Explanation: The well-known Tom Baker (the Doctor Who actor) has voiced roles in video games but is not known to have reviewed them. The name is common, so another Tom Baker may have written game reviews, but without that context the claim is misleading.

claim: Super Bowl XLV was played before February 6, 2011.
response_text: FALSE. Super Bowl XLV was played on February 6, 2011, not before that date.

claim: Henry II of France suffered an untimely death in 1567.
response_text: FALSE. Henry II of France died in 1559 from injuries sustained in a jousting accident (injured June 30, died July 10), not in 1567.

claim: Mount Rushmore was created by sculptor Tom Brady.
response_text: FALSE. Mount Rushmore was designed and carved by Gutzon Borglum (with work continued by his son Lincoln Borglum) between 1927 and 1941. Tom Brady is an NFL quarterback, not a sculptor involved with the monument.

claim: Bessie Smith lived out her days, from birth to death, on the fields of rural Germany.
response_text: FALSE. Bessie Smith was an American blues singer, born in Chattanooga, Tennessee (1894), who lived and worked in the United States and died in Mississippi (1937) after a car accident. She had no life based in rural Germany.

claim: The Adventures of Pluto Nash stars an actor that was born on February 5, 1961.
response_text: FALSE.  Explanation: The film stars Eddie Murphy (born April 3, 1961), Rosario Dawson (born May 9, 1979), and Randy Quaid (born October 1, 1950). None of the principal cast were born on February 5, 1961, and there’s no known cast member with that birthdate. (Slight uncertainty for obscure cameo roles, but no evidence supports the claim.)

claim: Anne Sullivan is known for being Helen Keller's instructor.
response_text: TRUE. Anne Sullivan (Anne Sullivan Macy) was Helen Keller’s teacher and lifelong companion, famed for teaching Keller to communicate; she is widely known as “the Miracle Worker.”

claim: General Motors only sells automotive components
response_text: FALSE.  General Motors sells complete vehicles (Chevrolet, GMC, Cadillac, Buick) and offers services like OnStar and GM Financial. Components/parts are only one part of its business, not the only thing it sells.

claim: The Columbia River undergoes drainage.
response_text: TRUE — Though awkwardly phrased, the Columbia River “drains” a large watershed (about 670,000 km²) across the Pacific Northwest and empties into the Pacific Ocean; in hydrology this is its drainage basin.

claim: Agent Raghav – Crime Branch was nominated for Best Weekend Show.
response_text: TRUE  Agent Raghav – Crime Branch received an Indian Television Academy Awards (ITA) nomination in 2015 for Best Weekend Show. (Slight uncertainty due to reliance on award listing recollection.)

claim: Sean Penn was in Fast Times at Ridgemont High in 1982.
response_text: TRUE. Sean Penn played Jeff Spicoli in the 1982 film Fast Times at Ridgemont High.

claim: A working animal can perform tasks after being trained.
response_text: TRUE. By definition, a working animal is trained to carry out tasks for humans (e.g., herding, guiding, pulling loads), so after training it can perform such tasks.

claim: Miranda Otto is the aunt of actress Gracie Otto.
response_text: FALSE. Miranda Otto and Gracie Otto are half-sisters (both daughters of actor Barry Otto), so Miranda is not Gracie’s aunt.

claim: Jenna Jameson started acting in erotic videos in 1990.
response_text: FALSE.  Jenna Jameson (born 1974) began her adult film career in the early 1990s, commonly cited as 1993 (around age 19), not 1990. In 1990 she would have been 16.

claim: Benzodiazepine is a medication.
response_text: TRUE. Benzodiazepines are a class of psychoactive medications (e.g., diazepam, lorazepam) used for anxiety, insomnia, seizures, and muscle relaxation. While “benzodiazepine” names the drug class/chemical structure, its members are medications.
